newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends softer at 489.25/490.25/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends softer at 489.25/490.25/dlr.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed weaker at 489.25/490.25 per dollar Monday as an increase in the Central Bank reserve requirement had little effect on market liquidity, traders said.
Traders said that banks had turned to the currency market after a new measure to raise the reserve requirement at the Central Bank from 12 to 15 percent had little effect on market liquidity.
"The effect of the new reserve requirement was not as expected and money markets remained liquid," one trader said.
Interbank overnight lending rates opened at 10 percent but later fell to about five percent, traders said.
Banks which sold dollars to meet the new reserve requirement in the morning "had to buy back their positions because the market remained very liquid," one trader said.
The Central Bank raised the reserve requirement last week to tackle an expected bubble of excess liquidity in coming weeks.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
Venezuela continues to pursue an inflation-fighting strong bolivar policy, where the currency ostensibly floats between slowly depreciating bands set by Central Bank intervention.
Critics say the policy has left the bolivar increasingly over-valued with the exchange rate little-changed since price and currency controls were removed in April last year.
